label: thm:chain
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:chain}
For every even $t \ge 4$ let $M = t^4$ and $r = t^3$, and consider the minimum-cost-flow LP on a path with return arcs $\min \sum_{i=1}^M u_i$ subject to $u_j - u_{j+1} - v_j = b_j$ ($1 \le j < M$), $u, v \ge 0$, with an explicit rational $b \in [0.97, 1.03]^{M-1}$. It has a unique nondegenerate optimal basis, and three dual-feasible starts satisfy, under exact DSE,
\begin{center}\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\small{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt{10pt}\ixpt\@ixpt
\begin{tabular}{lccc}\toprule
Start & Overlap with $B^\star$ & Pivots & Work $K$\\ \midrule
Cold (all-slack: every $v_j$ basic) & $0$ & $M-1$ & $\sim \tfrac32 t^6$\\
Warm A (last $r$ chain arcs missing: singletons) & $1 - r/(M-1)$ & $r$ & $\sim 2t^5$\\
Warm B (every second of the last $2r$ arcs missing: pairs) & $1 - r/(M-1)$ & $r$ & $\sim t^7$\\ \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Every choice on the three paths is unique, every basis factorizes without fill, and the two warm bases have equal nonzero counts after every pivot. Hence $K_B/K_A \sim t^2/2 = \Theta(\sqrt{M})$, and $K_B/K_{\text{cold}} = \Theta(M^{1/4})$.

name: Equal overlap and pivot count, unbounded work ratio

label: cor:proxy
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:proxy}
With $r-1$ missing arcs, warm B has strictly higher overlap and one fewer pivot than warm A, and still $\sim t^2/2$ times its work.
head: environment
name: The proxy-optimal start can be the costlier one

title: Algorithm
body_md: The nine shifts plus two strategy actions: the native solver, for LPs on which no learned start pays off, and the unshifted start continued with primal simplex, for starts that are nearly primal feasible. The policy over $\mathcal{A}_2$ is \textsc{CostStart-Alg}\xspace.

title: Results
body_md: Table~\ref{tab:luyanbench} in \S\ref{sec:luyan} gives the per-dataset results. The decision policy takes $0.58\times$ the iterations and $0.72\times$ {\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\scriptsize{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt[0.68,\,0.75]} the time of the dual simplex, against $1.03\times$ for our reimplementation of Lu \& Yan and $0.92\times$ for Fan et al. Paired, it takes $0.69\times$ {\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\@setsize\scriptsize{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt{8pt}\viipt\@viipt[0.64,\,0.75]} the time of Lu \& Yan (Mirp1 $0.48$, Anonymous $0.64$, Load balancing $0.74$, Mirp2 $1.03$) and $0.78\times$ that of Fan et al. Against our fine-tuned predictor with top-$m$ repair it takes $0.84\times$ the time at the same iterations ($1.02\times$), so the gain comes from cheaper decoding and cheaper iterations. The best single action per dataset alone reaches $0.73\times$, so on datasets this small most of the gain comes from choosing among decoders, algorithms and pricing rules by measured cost, not from a per-LP choice; initializing the policy from \textsc{CostStart-Full}\xspace, which was trained on our data, hurts ($0.86\times$).
